design_rationale:
WHY THIS MAKES A GOOD TEST. The caller asks for one thing — "challenge this damage in my name, properly, before anyone takes money off me" — and the challenge cannot be quantified until a problem he never raises has been resolved: the damage the rental desk approved is not yet on the rental's ledger, and the dispute policy's own rule says the amount a renter may put in dispute is fixed only once the ledger carries the entry for the damage the rental desk has approved against the rental. The agent must read that sentence, look at the ledger, see that the only damage recharge anywhere in this renter's world belongs to a different, closed rental, find the policy that raises the recharge, price it from six factors that reach into the rate class's waiver excess, the protection sold on the rental, how promptly the assessment was decided, the renter's own rental damage claims on another product and the value of the vehicle hired, raise it, and only then hand the challenge to the renter to put through in his own name with his own evidence reference. Nothing is a matter of picking between similar tools; the difficulty is seeing the hidden problem, reading eleven ladders off the records rather than off the caller, and getting two chained figures exactly right at two different handling times.

SCOPE (principle C). Task 1 claims: extended policies drive_ext_damage_recharge and drive_ext_recharge_dispute, and the task tools post_damage_recharge_2d59c35f (owner agent) and raise_recharge_dispute_65c619e1 (owner user), with base lineage drive_damage_and_recharges and drive_agg_rental_history. It occupies the post-return recharge side of this category. Task 0 occupies the cancellation-charge and refund-payout writes with lineage drive_cancellation, drive_prepayment and drive_refund_settlement. No policy, tool, base event subject or scored write is shared between the two, and together the two tasks cover every extended policy of this difficulty.

THE DRAW (Step 0, scripts/draw_counts.py env/online_travel_agency/tasks/car_rental_desk --task 1):
{"task": 1, "key": "online_travel_agency/car_rental_desk/1", "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [5, 6]}
One prerequisite problem, two problems in all, and the two computations declare five and six factors: drive_ext_damage_recharge takes the count of 6 and drive_ext_recharge_dispute the count of 5.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD.
Root problem: drive_ext_recharge_dispute — what the caller asks for, the challenge raised in his own name.
Prerequisite problem: drive_ext_damage_recharge — the recharge the approved assessment makes due, raised by the desk.
Edge: drive_ext_recharge_dispute <- drive_ext_damage_recharge. kind=value_input; gate=recharge_on_ledger (a real compute binding of the dispute policy); form=state; resolved_by=post_damage_recharge_2d59c35f (owner agent).
Prerequisite sentence (policy_source, verbatim from the dispute policy's own rule): "The amount a renter may put in dispute is fixed only once the ledger carries the entry for the damage the rental desk has approved against the rental."
Four-point test: (1) "only once" is the ordering connective, joining this policy's own result (the amount a renter may put in dispute) to what it waits on; (2) what it waits on is a record-visible state — the ledger carrying the entry for the approved damage — with no action, performer or tool named; (3) no tool name, policy id, snake_case token or row id appears in it; (4) it is exactly as strong and wide as the edge: a hard requirement over one kind of ledger entry on this rental, no wider and no narrower than the condition that a damage recharge line stands against it.
State form is available and used: exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about — post_damage_recharge_2d59c35f is the only tool in task_tools.py that creates a drive_rental_entries row whose charge_category is damage_charge. Derivation the reader performs: the dispute rule says the amount is fixed only once the ledger carries the entry for the approved damage; the rental's ledger carries rate days, a waiver, theft protection, a licensing fee, tax, a refuelling settlement, a cleaning charge and two mileage rows, and no damage recharge; the recharge policy's own rule says what is recharged for damage the desk has approved and how it is built; therefore the recharge must be priced and raised first, and the only action that raises it is that policy's own. Exactly one reading.
Why the condition is false at the opening: no row of initial_state.drive_rental_entries carries both this rental's drive_rental_id and charge_category damage_charge. The cleaning charge f9cb11ef is an event of the same family but carries charge_category cleaning_fee, which is precisely the near-miss: a reader who aggregates the damage event family rather than the damage charge category finds 125.00 where the rule means nothing. The one row in this world whose charge_category is damage_charge, c6b31d2d, carries drive_rental_id 95f1f2c4-290c-433e-a7de-0d6b4c245e55 — the renter's older, closed Seattle rental — so a reader who sums by customer rather than by rental finds 480.00 that is not there. The compute binding recharge_on_ledger is therefore 0.0 at the opening and 903.0 once the recharge lands.
Topological order: raise the recharge, then register the challenge. One edge, one possible order.
Deletion sensitivity (Step 5 run): skipping the recharge and replaying everything else leaves the challenge at 140.85 instead of 464.05 — the whole damage element of the challenge disappears and only the cleaning and fuel elements remain.
The tool layer blocks nothing: raise_recharge_dispute_65c619e1 is one ctx.make_id and one ctx.create; it never reads the ledger, never looks for a damage recharge, never tests a status and returns no policy-based error, so it registers whatever amount it is given whether or not the recharge stands. post_damage_recharge_2d59c35f is the same shape. Only the terminal hash records the difference.
user_scenario mentions no prerequisite: the caller says the rental company wrote holding him responsible and asks for the matter to be challenged in his name. He never mentions a charge on his account, never asks what the recharge comes to, and drops no hint that anything must be raised first; his contribution on that side is entirely passive, accepting the explanation when the agent gives it and running the challenge when it is handed to him.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Both writes have the same exact subject, drive_damage_charge, and the same single governing base policy, drive_damage_and_recharges, whose three eligibility gates are inherited item by item into both steps.
- vehicle_out_or_returned ("A recharge is raised only while the rental record stands at picked up or returned."): the official row initial_state.drive_rentals.c390c49a...status = returned, correlated to each write through drive_rentals.drive_rental_id, which the gate's action_bindings pins to the tools' drive_rental_id argument.
- damage_assessment_approved ("Damage is recharged only when the rental desk has already recorded an approved damage assessment against this rental."): the review row 5e463211 stands at approved, decided 2026-08-22 16:40:00 PDT, correlated through drive_damage_reviews.drive_review_id, which the gate pins to the tools' drive_review_id argument. The second review on the rental, 1bbc723f, is a fuel dispute standing declined; it satisfies nothing and is the excludable trap for an agent who reads "a review exists" as "an assessment is approved".
- inside_damage_window (time): frozen time 2026-08-24 14:30:00 PDT is not after the moment the renter returned the vehicle, 2026-08-15 08:45:00 PDT, plus the rate class's damage reporting window of ten calendar days. temporal_feasibility copies the base contract verbatim for both steps — clock frozen_time, anchor event "the moment the renter returned the vehicle to the supplier", anchor source drive_rentals.returned_at, relation not_after, duration variants.damage_report_window_days, unit calendar_days, the counting rule counted from the day after the return date with the closing day still in time, boundary inclusive. Boundary cases: counted from the day after 2026-08-15, the tenth day is 2026-08-25, so a recharge raised at any moment of 2026-08-25 is still in time and one raised on 2026-08-26 is out; the world sits one day inside that closing day, and had the rate class been the Inclusive Flex Rate with its seven-day window the closing day would have been 2026-08-22 and both writes would already be barred.
Other clauses of drive_damage_and_recharges are honoured rather than overridden, which is why overwrite is empty on both policies: damage is recharged up to the rate class's waiver excess where the waiver was carried (the excess is the root of the recharge and the seed carries a waiver sold on the rental); the administration charge is added once per incident and never once per damaged part (the administration element is a single element, scaled only by the reopening of a declined review, never by parts); soiling is settled as a recharge rather than as damage (the cleaning charge already stands as its own line and never enters the damage aggregate); and a renter who disputes a recharge is referred to a review with the disputed amount left standing on the ledger (which is exactly the terminal state gold produces: the recharge stands and the challenge is open beside it).

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. The object is one rental: c390c49a-49ea-4764-8f9c-9d8d3ac9cc97, agreement RA5028741, Pay At Counter Flex Rate, five charged days out of the Portland downtown branch, returned 2026-08-15. The correlation key is drive_rental_id, carried by every ledger row and every review and taken as an argument by both tools; the incident is further keyed by drive_review_id, so the recharge and the challenge both name the assessment 5e463211 and no other. Rows that enter the aggregates: five rental-rate days at 54.00, the waiver at 129.95, theft protection at 59.95, the cleaning charge at 125.00 and the refuelling settlement at 63.39. Rows on the same rental that are read but deliberately excluded: the licensing fee, the sales tax, the agency service fee and the two mileage rows, none of which any rule aggregates. Rows on the same customer excluded by drive_rental_id: the whole of the older Seattle rental 95f1f2c4 and its five ledger rows, including its 480.00 damage recharge. Nothing on this rental has been settled or reversed: there is no payout line, so the dispute's settled-payout branch does not apply.

WHY EACH CLASS OF SEED ROW EXISTS.
customers/d981962f: the caller; his mobile number and passport digits are what the identity check consumes.
drive_rentals/c390c49a: the target rental. status returned satisfies the first gate; returned_at anchors both the window gate and the two date spans that decide the report share and the timing share; rental_days 5 turns the rate lines into 54.00 a day, which sits between the mid and high day rates; mileage_allowance_remaining 140 is what puts the cleaning element on its first tier; the rate class booked supplies the waiver excess of 950.00, the administration charge of 95.00 and the ten-day reporting window. Change any one and both scored numbers move.
drive_rentals/95f1f2c4: a second holding in this category, closed, carrying the near-miss damage recharge described above and a consistent prepaid Saver-rate history of its own.
drive_rental_entries: five rental-day lines at the class's own daily rate (a rental of fewer than seven days with no weekend day in it, so the daily rate applies to each); the waiver and theft protection sold at collection at the class's own per-day amounts over five days (129.95 and 59.95), which decide the excess relief and the whole protection deduction; the licensing recovery fee at the class's per-day amount over five days; the sales tax at the class's rate on the rental rate; the refuelling settlement of 63.39, which is the fuel element of the challenge; the cleaning charge of 125.00, settled as a recharge rather than as damage exactly as base prescribes, which is the cleaning element of the challenge and the near-miss for the damage aggregate; the mileage grant of 1000 and consumption of 860, which leave the 140 miles the cleaning ladder reads; and the agency service fee charged once when the supplier confirmed.
drive_damage_reviews/5e463211: the approved damage assessment. It is the authorisation the second gate requires, its decided_at is the date both timing ladders measure to, and its evidence reference is what the recharge line quotes.
drive_damage_reviews/1bbc723f: the declined fuel dispute. It is load-bearing three times over — it puts the administration element on its reopened tier, it puts the amount open to challenge on its "a review already stands declined" tier, and it puts the fuel element on its reopened-share tier — and it is the trap for an agent who treats any review as an approved assessment.
club_memberships/021b108f: the Silver membership, active, whose car rental discount of 3 per cent is the relief on the excess borne. Remove it and the recharge rises to 932.62.
care_policies/e265fe72: the TripGuard Plus policy in force over the whole August trip. Its rental damage benefit decides the loading condition on the recharge and, through its limit and deductible, the part of the challenge that travel protection answers. care_policies/3628ffb0 is the expired 2025 policy the earlier claim was filed under, seeded so that the claim has a real parent.
care_claims/fd5eec81: one rental damage claim filed 2025-09-14, eleven months before frozen time and therefore inside the twenty-four-month window, arising from the 480.00 damage recharge on the older rental. It is the cross-difficulty evidence the recharge's loading rests on; delete it and the recharge falls to 833.86.
Automatic-clause check: nothing fires unattended. The vehicle came back before its booked return, so no extra-hour or extra-day charge is owed; the miles driven are inside the allowance granted, so no excess mileage is owed; the fuel settlement and the cleaning charge already stand; both rentals' charges_total_usd and mileage_allowance_remaining are exactly the sums of their ledger deltas (703.12 and 140; 610.45 and 95). No cache trap is used.

PERSONA DESIGN. Tomas is flat, unhurried and used to arguing about estimates; the voice is that of somebody who reads slips rather than feelings. He volunteers the surface goal (challenge it, in my name, on the record, before money moves), the natural circumstances (five days in August, the counter walk-round, the supplier's letter the Saturday after the return, reaching him a couple of days before the call) and one hard preference (he will not pay quietly and argue later). Identity comes only when asked, in the order a real caller offers it. His evidence reference, the return inspection slip PDX-RET-40912, is given only when the agent asks what he has to support the challenge, and it is the verbatim source of the tool's evidence argument. Everything about the prerequisite is passive: only after the agent explains that the assessment is approved, that the charge therefore goes on the rental, and that it stays there while the challenge is looked at, does he accept it and run the challenge when it is handed over. The natural traps are that he mentions the earlier refuelling row only if asked and will not say what he thinks it means, and that he may once call a figure "a lot for a scuff" and ask for it to be checked without having any view of what it should be.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate and verify; read the rentals and take the returned Portland one; read the ledger and separate its rows from the older rental's; read the reviews and see one approved assessment and one declined fuel dispute; read the membership (Silver, active) and the protection policies (TripGuard Plus in force, plus an expired 2025 policy) and the claims (one rental damage claim filed 2025-09-14). Then price the recharge: the waiver stands sold on the rental and the membership carries a 3 per cent car rental discount, so the excess borne is 950.00 less 3 per cent, 921.50; both the waiver and theft protection stand sold, so what was paid for both, 189.90, comes off, leaving 731.60; the approved assessment was decided on 2026-08-22, seven calendar days after the 2026-08-15 return and so within the eight prompt report days, so 90 per cent of it is recharged, 658.44; one rental damage claim in the last twenty-four months carries the single claim loading of 10 per cent, 724.284; the rate charged works out at 54.00 a day, above the mid day rate of 45 and not above the high day rate of 75, so the mid uplift of 5 per cent applies, 760.4982; one damage assessment stands approved, so the administration charge is not multiplied by a count of incidents, and the damage was decided within the eight prompt report days with a review already standing declined, so the administration charge of 95.00 is added at the reopened multiple, 142.50; rounded once, 903.00. Raise it against the approved assessment, quoting its supplier reference. Then price the challenge on the world as it now stands: the ledger carries one damage recharge and a review stands declined, so the amount open to challenge is 903.00 less the 95.00 administration charge, 808.00; the policy in force carries a rental damage limit of 25000.00, above that amount, and a deductible, so the insured share of 60 per cent, 484.80, is answered by it, leaving 323.20; three times the seven days of window used, 21, is more than twice the ten-day window, so the whole of it is left open; the ledger carries a cleaning charge of 125.00 and the mileage still unused is 140, so the whole of the cleaning charge is added; the ledger carries a refuelling settlement of 63.39 and a fuel dispute stands declined against the rental, so a quarter of it, 15.8475, is added; rounded once, 464.05. Hand that to the renter to put through with his slip number.

VERIFICATION ACTUALLY RUN (Step 5). Evaluated with the gate's own primitives (build_env / eval_compute from skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/check_compute.py) against initial_state at frozen time, then the recharge tool executed on a seeded DB and the dispute evaluated against the resulting world. Output:
  drive_ext_damage_recharge: result=903.0 (club_rental_discount_pct=3, waiver_sold_total=129.95, excess_borne=921.5, theft_sold_total=59.95, protection_offset=189.9, assessment_decided_on=2026-08-22 16:40:00 PDT, days_to_decision=7, report_share_pct=90, damage_claims_24m=1, protection_in_force=True, history_loading_pct=10, rate_lines_total=270.0, day_rate_charged=54.0, vehicle_uplift_pct=5, approved_assessments=1, declined_reviews=1, admin_element=142.5, borne_after_protection=731.6, after_report_share=658.44, after_loading=724.284, after_value=760.4982)
    factor baselines: excess_borne_relief=932.62, protection_deduction=1100.4, report_promptness=776.25, claim_record_loading=833.86, vehicle_value_uplift=866.78, administration_element=855.5; every one moves the result. All baselines at once = 807.5.
  drive_ext_recharge_dispute: result=464.05 (recharge_on_ledger=903.0, declined_reviews=1, damage_lines_count=1, disputable_base=808.0, protection_limit=25000.0, protection_deductible=250.0, insured_part=484.8, after_insurance=323.2, window_days_used=7, window_share_pct=100, after_share=323.2, cleaning_on_ledger=125.0, miles_remaining=140, cleaning_element=125.0, fuel_on_ledger=63.39, fuel_disputes_declined=1, fuel_element=15.8475)

  prerequisite sensitivity: the challenge recomputed with the recharge skipped = 140.85 against 464.05.
Both figures equal the gold arguments and the declared expected values exactly.

RULE/COMPUTE TWO-WAY SWEEP. Forward: every binding that reads the world, aggregates, chooses, crosses categories, caps or rounds quotes its rule sentence verbatim in compute_basis — the four ledger aggregates and the two review counts, the two date spans, each of the eleven ladders, and the floor and rounding sentences. Backward: reading each rule through, every load-bearing sentence is claimed by a binding — in the recharge rule the excess and its two reliefs (excess_borne), the protection deduction and its floor at nothing (protection_offset, borne_after_protection), the day-count convention and the three report shares (days_to_decision, report_share_pct), the two loadings (history_loading_pct), the two uplifts and the order in which they act (vehicle_uplift_pct, after_value), the administration element and its three cases (admin_element) and the single rounding after the administration charge (result); in the dispute rule the three measures of the amount open to challenge (disputable_base), the two insured shares and the floor after them (insured_part, after_insurance), the day-count and the three timing shares (window_days_used, window_share_pct), the cleaning ladder (cleaning_element), the fuel ladder (fuel_element) and the floor and rounding (result). The acting base is written out in prose in both rules, as is the order of operations (the protection deduction before the share, the share before the loading, the loading before the uplift, the administration charge added last and only then rounded; the insurance taken off the amount open to challenge before the timing share is applied, and the cleaning and fuel elements added after it), and both interval conventions are spelled out as calendar days from the return date to the decision date.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT. Masking the extended YAML, compute, expected, gold and this dossier, and working only from the documents that will be published, the tool schemas, the rows the finders return and what the caller actually says: the caller wants the damage challenged; the dispute document says the amount is fixed only once the ledger carries the entry for the approved damage; the ledger carries no such entry; the recharge document gives a complete method whose every input the records supply; the recharge is raised against the approved assessment, and the challenge follows, in the renter's own name because it is his challenge to make. The same two numbers come out. The places a careless reader diverges are all excludable from the documents and the records: counting the cleaning charge as recharged damage (125.00 that the damage aggregate does not carry), counting the older rental's 480.00, treating the declined fuel dispute as the approved assessment, measuring the seven days from the booked return rather than the actual return, and taking the fuel element in full where a fuel dispute already stands declined.

CLOSURE. policy -> target_tool -> computation -> GT call -> terminal state: drive_ext_damage_recharge -> post_damage_recharge_2d59c35f -> computations[0] (step 9, damage_recharge_usd = 903.0) -> the ledger row ddc_... standing against the rental and quoting the supplier's damage reference; drive_ext_recharge_dispute -> raise_recharge_dispute_65c619e1 -> computations[1] (step 11, disputed_amount_usd = 464.05) -> the review row drv_... standing submitted and undecided beside it, with the renter's own slip number recorded. charter_scope, required_documents and the computations' policy ids are the same two ids in the same order, and gold calls exactly those two tools in the topological order of the tree.


REWORK — ROUND 2, against env/online_travel_agency/audits/policy_task/car_rental_desk/1.md and _difficulty.md.
Every finding of the audit that bears on this task is answered below. No scored value moved: the recharge is still 903.00, the challenge still 464.05, every factor-sensitivity figure and both whole-baseline figures are unchanged, and the skip-effect is still 140.85. The Step 5 verification was re-run after the changes and reproduced all of them.

1-1 / F-2 (RED, undeclared override of "The class's damage administration charge is added once per incident and never once per damaged part."). CLOSED by declaring the override. `drive_ext_damage_recharge.overwrite` now carries an entry naming `drive_damage_and_recharges`, quoting that sentence verbatim as `superseded_clause`, and quoting this policy's own administration paragraph as `replaced_by`. The declaration makes the deviation traceable at the clause it replaces, which is what the "anonymous intermediate factor" pattern hid: the reopened administration multiple is now legislated rather than smuggled in through a multiplier, so the recharge has one defensible figure, 903.00, and the challenge that reads it one defensible figure, 464.05. The declaration retires no eligibility gate — the superseded sentence neither contains nor is contained in any of the three gate conditions — so all three base preconditions are still inherited and still evidenced in `solvability_contract`, and both temporal_feasibility entries stand.

1-2 (observation, the persona's "ten days later" cannot be true at frozen time). CLOSED in the persona: the letter is now "The Saturday after that ... and the letter reached him a couple of days ago", which is 2026-08-22 — the day the rental desk decided the assessment, `drive_damage_reviews/5e463211-….decided_at` — reaching him before frozen time 2026-08-24 14:30. The caller's own account of the dates now agrees with the record he is not able to read, so the two ladders that turn on that date (`report_promptness` at seven days against eight, `assessment_timing_share` at seven times three against ten times two) can no longer be pushed to a wrong tier by believing him. No scored value moves, because every input still reads the record.

1-3 / F-6 (observation, the extended damage basis ignores whether the waiver was carried). CLOSED by declaring the override. `drive_ext_damage_recharge.overwrite` carries a second entry quoting base's "Damage discovered at return or afterwards is recharged to the renter up to the rate class's waiver excess where the waiver was carried, and in full where it was not." and naming this policy's own sentence "The excess the renter bears is the rate class's waiver excess." as what takes its place. The extended policy therefore says outright that it works from the waiver excess whatever the rental carried, and the base limb that would demand a quantity this policy has no input for is retired by declaration rather than left standing in silent conflict. On this world the rental did carry the waiver, so nothing moves; on a world without one there is now a single reading.

1-4 / O-2 (observation, the claims loading does not say where the claims were filed). CLOSED in the rule: every sentence of the loading ladder, and the opening sentence that lists what the recharge is built from, now read "rental damage claims filed on their travel protection policies", matching `XCOUNT('care','care_claims', …, claim_type='rental_damage')` exactly. The drive-side measure `drive_msr_damage_claims_24m` is no longer a candidate reading, and base `drive_agg_rental_history`'s "history across rentals decides two things and nothing else" is no longer in tension with it, because the loading is now plainly keyed to the protection ledger and not to the rental history. Both readings gave 1 on this world, so the figure is unchanged.

1-5 / O-3 (observation, `administration_element`'s first tier is unreachable given the base gate). CLOSED by replacing that tier with a reachable, base-compliant one: "Where more than one damage assessment stands approved against the rental the administration charge is added once for each approved assessment" — which is base's own "once per incident" read across several incidents, and which the compute implements through a new binding `approved_assessments` (a count of approved reviews on the rental). The dropped branch "beyond the reporting window", which the inherited `inside_damage_window` gate already made unreachable, is gone. This world carries exactly one approved assessment, so the tier taken is unchanged, the administration element is still 142.50 and the recharge still 903.00.

1-6 / O-6 (observation, the dispute policy's subject does not name the record its tool writes). ANSWERED, no change. `subject` must name a declared event of this category, and the difficulty's claimed event types carry no review-creation event; `drive_damage_charge` is the event the challenge is raised against and is what fixes the three base gates the write inherits — the rental's state, the approved assessment, and the reporting window — all of which genuinely govern who may challenge what and until when. Naming any other event would either misdescribe the write or drop those gates. The write itself is honest about what it touches: the tool creates one `drive_damage_reviews` row and posts no ledger line, as base's "A renter who disputes a recharge is referred to a review, and the disputed amount stays on the ledger until the review decides it" requires.

1-7 (no finding on the derivation). Noted; nothing in this rework moved any derived value, and the Step 5 re-run confirms it figure for figure.

O-1 (ladders ordered rather than pairwise disjoint as stated). CLOSED in prose: both of this task's policies now end their rules with "Where more than one of the cases stated here fits a rental, the case stated earliest in this rule applies to that rental and the others do not.", so the first-match convention the compute implements is legislated and an overlapping pair of tiers cannot be read two ways.

O-5 (base's "until the review decides it" states an order that grounds no declared edge). ANSWERED, no change. The sentence is base's and base is frozen; it orders a dispute against a review decision that no policy of this difficulty writes, so it grounds no edge and no task's tree rests on it. This policy carries its own prerequisite sentence for the one edge it does declare, and that sentence is about a ledger entry, not about a decision.

F-1, F-3, F-4, F-5, 0-3 and 0-4 bear on task 0's policies and are answered in that task's dossier. O-4 is answered there too; this task already reads `care`, the `travel_protection_desk` difficulty, in two factors. O-7 is a harness observation about the replay gate's write-back and is reported to the coordinator rather than fixed here.

user_scenario:
Tomas Ferreira runs the service side of a small marine engineering outfit in Portland and has the flat, unhurried manner of somebody who spends his days arguing about other people's estimates. He hired a car for five days in August while his own van was in the shop, dropped it back at the downtown branch on the Saturday morning, and had the counter staff walk round it with him. The Saturday after that the rental company wrote to say they were holding him responsible for damage to the offside rear of the vehicle, and the letter reached him a couple of days ago. He does not accept it, and that is why he is calling: he wants the thing formally challenged, in his name, so that it is on record and somebody has to look at it properly before anyone takes money off him. He is not asking for a refund, he is not asking anybody to lean on the supplier, and he is quite clear that he is not going to pay it quietly and argue later.

He gives his name, Tomas Ferreira, at the start, along with the mobile number the booking notifications go to, 7040562137. If he is asked for more before anything can be discussed he gives his date of birth as 1982-11-02 and the last four of his passport as 4318; if the agent still wants something he offers his billing postcode, 97209. The agreement number on the rental was RA5028741, which he reads out if asked, and he will confirm the dates as the tenth to the fifteenth of August out of the Portland downtown branch.

The point he keeps coming back to, without dressing it up, is that the vehicle was checked in with him standing there and the slip he was given says nothing about the offside rear. When the agent asks what he has to support the challenge, he reads out the return inspection slip number, PDX-RET-40912, and says the branch printed it for him at the desk on the Saturday. He does not have photographs and says so plainly if he is asked. He also mentions, only if the agent raises the state of the account or asks whether anything else is in dispute, that he already had a row with them about a refuelling charge on the same rental and was told no; he will not say what he thinks that means for this.

He holds a Wanderlane card and, asked about it, says he is Silver and reads the membership number WL-2208-6647. If the agent asks whether he has any travel insurance he says yes, he took a TripGuard policy for the whole August trip, certificate TG-2026-884512, and adds that he has no idea whether that is relevant and would rather the desk told him than he guessed.

He does not know how the desk works out what he is being held responsible for, and he never asks for the figure in advance. If the agent explains that the assessment has been approved on the supplier's side, that the charge therefore has to go on the rental before anything can be challenged, and that the amount stays there while the challenge is looked at, he says that is not what he would have chosen but he understands it and to carry on. When the agent hands the challenge over for him to put through in his own name, he does it there and then and reads back what comes up. If, at the end, he is told the challenge is open with the rental desk, he asks how long these usually take, thanks them for doing it properly, and rings off.

If at any point the figure he is shown strikes him as high he will say once that it sounds like a lot for a scuff and ask the agent to check it against what the rental actually was, but he has no view of his own on what it should be and takes the second answer as given. He never quotes terms, never suggests what ought to be taken off, and if the agent gets something wrong he has no way of knowing it. Anything about what the supplier's inspector actually saw, how the body shop priced it, or where the insurer stands, he says straight out that he cannot answer and leaves with the desk.
